- FACES (worked out from the model files): a prop's group turns PI - face; a +z front looks compass `face` (0 north, 90 east); a +x front looks
  (-cos, -sin) of face. Benches, vending machines, the shelter (before its turn), utility_box: +z. Road signs, bus_stop_sign, ind_vent, ind_panel: +x.

## THE STEEL LANDING — a fire escape's platform, no terrain lump (2026-11-13)
mondo: "wherever there are ladders, there is a raised piece of terrain to go with it that looks wrong, and its easy to fall off of and i can
climb it just by jumping up next to it ... Can i not just climb up the ladder and stand on the platform part?" He picked "Steel platform you
stand on". The lump was the fire escape's halfway LANDING, a 1.6 x 2.2 m terrain `plateau` (the height field can only draw it as a slanted
block). 25 of them, city rooms only: `site_prebuilt_downtown_streets` 18 (bake-disaster-city.js, the `escapeAt` loop),
`site_prebuilt_cyberpunk_streets` 5 (STACK W + E1 had a second, wider plateau for the stair's head: one landing each now, 4 rows),
`site_prebuilt_downtown_oldstreets` 2. Every other ladder in the game climbs straight onto a real tier.
- **The row**: `{ k: 'landing', x, z, w, d, h | y, back, gaps? }` (data.js `hqTerrainLandings`, compiled in `hqTerrainCompile` before the first
  `hqTerrainClimbs`): `h` over the LOWEST ground under it (or absolute `y`), `back` = the heading of the building's side (no rail),
  `gaps: [[heading, a, b]]` = a stair's mouth in a rail. It becomes a hidden `bridge` slab (`hide`, `landing`, 0.1 thick: the ground under it
  stays flat and walked) + one hung `ghost` wall per open side (`y0` = the slab, 1.05 high: the walker cannot step off). A landing with no
  mass behind it (its building became a walk-in: P01-08-B1) gets an unseen wall on the back too (`guard`).
- **The ladders**: `hqTerrainClimbs` gives a foot / a head on a landing the slab's height (`c.footOn` / `c.landing`); `hqTerrainClimbEdges`
  takes for such an end the nearest grid node that STANDS on the slab (the nearest node may lie under a rail: two city landings fell out of
  the reach until this).
- **The look** (three-renderer.js `_hqBuildClimbs`, after the ladders): an iron deck + a grating, posts and two rails along each `rails` run
  (open where a ladder's head stands on that side), two struts to the wall; two merged meshes a landing. A fireescape ladder whose head is on a
  landing draws no cage of its own and ends in two grab rails.
- Checked offline (node, the compiled rooms, against main): same ladders, same reach flags on every ladder end, the same tapes with the same
  `hard` flags in the three rooms; standing on each slab, the ground under it, every rail blocks. NOT SEEN ON SCREEN (RULE #1c).
- After merging main in Disaster City: `node bake-disaster-city.js` (the tool writes the `landing` rows).

### THE FLUSH LANDING — the platform is level with the roof, you walk straight on (2026-11-15)
mondo: "They dont reach up all the way, so i cant even jump from the platform to the building to get on top. I should just be able to walk
off the platform and on to the roof/floor. But when i walk off the platform now, i fall off and clip into the building." Three causes:
the Disaster City platform was a HALFWAY landing (3.5 m, a second ladder on the wall went on to the 7 m roof); the hidden slab ended AT the
wall and its rim is not stood on (`bridgeEdge`), so the walker dropped down the strip between slab and wall; and a yard hedge along a
building's foot reached in over the roof's edge and set a roof walker down on the hedge's top, inside the building.
- **`flush: true`** on a `landing` row (data.js `hqTerrainLandings`): its top = the tier behind its `back` (the roof), no back guard, the
  result carries `flush`. With no tier behind it (the building became a walk-in: landings 0 and 10, P01-08-B1 and P06-05-B1) it keeps `h`.
  bake-disaster-city.js writes every fire escape as ONE flush landing + ONE ladder from the yard (the second ladder is gone: it would rise 0 m).
- **The lap**: every landing with a mass behind it runs its hidden slab 0.6 m into that mass (all three city rooms): a halfway landing's
  walker stops at the wall, a flush landing's walks onto the roof.
- **The mouth** (data.js `_hqTLandingMouths`, run on `info.arch` at compile, the room's rows never written): where a flush landing meets
  its roof, plain `box` parts on the roof's edge (the landing's width, 0.5 m out to 0.6 m in, up to 1.3 m over the roof) are cut along the
  edge (a parapet, a coping, a rail up to 0.7 m thick) or lose that stretch of one face (a roof-wide hollow rim, `top: false`). A district
  needs no gap of its own. Not cut: masses, quads, rings, parts turned off the square.
- **hqTerrainFeet**: a wall whose top is under the ground at that spot is no wall (the hedge under a roof's edge).
- Southside P05-08-B1: one roof AC unit stood in the mouth, moved 0.9 m along the edge (districts/S.js).
- Checked offline (node, the compiled room): all 16 flush landings are level with their roof, a walk off the back in 5 lanes reaches the roof
  with no drop (one lane set stops 2.5 m in at University P01-04-B1's own roof structure), the three railed sides still block, every roof
  is in the reach. Cyberpunk streets + the old streets keep their halfway landings and upper ladders (the stair heads need them); the
  walker there now stops at the wall. NOT SEEN ON SCREEN (RULE #1c). Known: Industrial P01-08-B2's drawn roof cap is 0.25 m over its walked roof.

## PLOT DUNGEONS — the puzzle dungeon vertical slices (2026-11-14, PLAN, mondo's answers in)
mondo uploaded two prototype packs from another chat (a PDF atlas + an HTML design pack, copies in /mnt/project-files/dungeons/source/)
and asked for one plan to build them as a standalone mode from the main menu or Settings. The plan is **docs/PLOT_DUNGEONS_PLAN.md**
(also /mnt/project-files/dungeons/): five 3 x 3 boards of 42 m plots (ROTATE catacombs, SLIDE Disaster City, CONNECT THE WORKS,
GROW AND CARRY fairy forest, ESCORT H-Wing), each plot a stage part moved by a live pose, Phase 0 = the engine proof.
AMENDED 11-14 09:32 (mondo): a standalone TEST build of ALL TEN pack designs (Settings > Developer > Open Plot Dungeons), dungeons
join story mode later (the old "no puzzles" lines in other docs do not apply to them), recommendations taken as decisions (plan §13), enemies are zone placeholders and
no dungeon type is tied to a place. Its §14 is the log: append one line there per phase, phase notes here.

### PLOT DUNGEONS, THE BUILD (2026-11-14, all ten prototypes, PR of thread "Build the puzzle dungeons")
**The way in:** Settings > Developer > Open Plot Dungeons (the level list, SOLVED marks, START OVER), or `?pd=<level>` in the URL
(crypt1, tomb1, street1, channel1, door1, connect1, rail1, worlds1, root1, escort1; `spike1` = the hidden engine proof).
**To tweak a dungeon or add a harder level** edit data.js between `PD-LEVELS-BEGIN` / `PD-LEVELS-END`, then `node bake-dungeons.js`:
- `PD_DUNGEONS.<type>.levels[]`: one row per level. The first is the prototype; a harder level is ONE MORE ROW (it shows in the list
  as LEVEL 2 by itself, its id is `<type>2`). Nothing else changes: no room block, no bake, no new file.
- A level = `plots` (each 12 strings of 12 squares + `marks`), `board` (slot → plot at the start; slots past the 3 x 3 such as B0 / B4
  hold fixed parts beside it), `rot` (start turns), `vacant` (the slots a slide may use), `entry`, `goal` (the checker's condition),
  and optionally `tokens`, `grows`, `keep`, `safe`.
- Squares: `#` mass, `.` floor, `o` whole-square blocker (the look's or the plot's `cover` prop), `=` the +7 m deck, `/` a flight
  (it climbs toward the deck beside it; `climb: { 'x,y': 'n' }` says otherwise), `~` water (walked, not drawn yet), space = a drop.
- A port is squares 5-6 of an edge. `ports: { ground: 'ew', upper: 'n' }` overrides what the squares say (an open machine floor).
  `net: { trace: 'ns' }` gives a plot ports on a layer nobody walks (a trace, a pipe, a track).
- A plot moves when its row says `turn: true` (or `{ detents: [0, 2] }`, `{ dirs: [1] }`) / `slide: true`; `turnWhen` / `slideWhen`
  are conditions; `ride: false` = nobody may stand on it while it moves.
- Marks (data.js pdRoomDef lists every field): spawn, dial / console / model (the board panel), prop, act (anything you press E on:
  `needs`, `no`, `say`, `set`, `give`, `fight`, `send`, `route`, `rotTo`), take (an item), gate (bars; `needs` + E, or `auto`),
  exit (walking there solves it), fight (the stand-in), trace / lamp / box (drawn, may be `lit` / `show` by a condition), rail.
- Conditions (data.js pdCheck): `{ has }`, `{ fight }`, `{ var, eq }`, `{ net, from, to }`, `{ joined: [plot, side, layer] }`,
  `{ link: [a, b] }`, `{ rot, eq }`, `{ slot, plot }`, `{ all }` (or a plain list), `{ any }`, `{ not }`.
- Looks: `PD_LOOKS` (the sheets, mood and wall kind of an existing room; a dungeon type is NOT tied to a look: change `look`).
**How it works:** data.js `pdInstall()` builds every plot's room (`pd_<level>_<plot>`, a box room with a drawn floor plan) and one
stage zone per level at load. The live board is `pdState` (slots, rot, vars, items, fights); `pdSync` writes the parts' frames and
the joins into the zone so the stage's own readers see it. three-renderer.js `hq.pd` tweens the parts (the current part is the scene's
origin, so when the plot under you turns the rest of the board, the sky and the key light swing the other way), builds the drawn rows
(`_hqPdBuild`: caps, jambs, bars, traces, lamps, blockers; never batched or instanced) and shows / lights / un-blocks them from
the board ~3 times a second (`_hqPdApply`). map.js holds the panel, the presses (`_pdAct` → data.js `pdDoAct`), the exit ring, the save
(localStorage `ew-pd-save-v1`, apart from the story's) and the launcher. Single player only; nothing is on `state` or relayed.
**`node bake-dungeons.js [level]`** (repo tooling, writes nothing): checks the grammar and searches each level's `goal` breadth first
over the board's own rules, printing the shortest solution. It ignores where the officer stands; the walk is proven in the browser.
**Proven in the browser 11-14** (officer walked, shots in /mnt/project-files/dungeons/proof/): all ten, start to exit.
**Honest limits of this first build:** (1) fights are STAND-INS: the mark lists the placeholder enemies, pressing FIGHT counts it as
won; the real field fight (hqEncounterLaunch on the fixed plot) is the next step. (2) The guardian of The Procession is the
angel statue prop that appears stop to stop (no walk cycle, no golem body yet). (3) Three Little Worlds is flat: the marbles are lit
blocks, no rolling, no 1.75 m height steps. (4) Missing Channel has no drawn water, the pipe lights instead. (5) Rubble plots are
plain paved blocks with a wreck. (6) The 3 x 3 model is the panel's drawing, the in-world table is a map table prop. (7) The plots
have no decor pass and the closed looks are dim. (8) The world clock runs, so an open look can be at night.

### PLOT DUNGEONS, THE SECOND PASS (2026-11-15, mondo: "there need to be buttons or levers or gears ... we dont even need this console thing")
His complaints after the first four: text lists of moves in a console, one console moving everything, collision on the skateboard,
lights switching on as you walk, no wide view when a plot moves. What changed (this supersedes the panel, the dial / console / model
marks and limits 6-8 above):
- **NO PANEL, NO LISTS.** The `dial` / `console` / `model` marks and map.js's board panel are gone. A move is a LEVER you pull:
  the `lever` mark `{ k: 'lever', x, y, plot?, by | track | dir, y3?, no? }`. ONE lever = ONE move of ONE plot (its own unless
  `plot` names another): `by: 1 | -1` a quarter turn left | right, `track: ['C3', 'B3', 'B2']` a slide along those slots (one slot
  a pull, back at the ends; every slot of a track must be in the level's `vacant`), `dir` a slide that way. data.js `pdDoAct`
  runs it (`A.move`), so a lever is an `act` like a valve. Its lamp and the strips at its plot's doors wear the plot's colour
  (`pdTint`, PD_RULES.tints). A button or a bell is an `act` with `stand: true` (a drawn stand under a wall piece).
- **YOU RIDE.** `pdMoveBlocked` no longer asks you to stand in the middle or to step off a sliding plot: the plot under your feet
  is the frame you stand in. Only `ride: false` plots refuse (their levers stand on other plots). Levers are spread so you walk
  (or ride) to each: see each level's comment in data.js.
- **THE WIDE VIEW** (PD_RULES.wide; three-renderer.js `_hqPdWideCam`): on every move the eye rises over the whole board, the plot
  moves, the eye waits and comes back. It is fixed to the BOARD (placed through the current part's frame of that frame), so a
  plot you ride is seen turning. Ceilings and fog are put away while it is up. A second pull while it is up keeps it up.
- **THE BOARD ROLLS ACROSS PLOTS.** `_hqStageCross` returned while riding, so a skater rolled into the next plot with the last
  plot's collision (walls you pass through, walls you cannot see). In a pd room the crossing now runs on the board too
  (`H.ride.hd` turns with the frame in `_hqStageSwap`).
- **THE SEAM IS THE WHOLE DOORWAY.** The stage keeps a walker `pad` metres inside a joined span's ends, so the outer metre of
  every 7 m doorway was a wall you could not see. `pdSync` now writes the span `PD_RULES.seamPad` wider each side.
  RULE: a plot's edge is crossed through squares 5-6 only; `bake-dungeons.js` fails a walked edge square outside them
  (a piece that is never walked says `edgeOk: true`).
- **LIGHT.** The stage lights 12 point lights at most (the nearest), which is why a side lit up as you came near. A closed level
  now has PD_RULES.lamps in all, its props' own lights counted (`pdPropLights`), so every lamp is always lit; the room light
  carries the rest (PD_RULES.ambient 1.5, lampK 1.6). An open look is locked at PD_RULES.hour (13:00); the forest look takes
  the city's day sky (`skyFrom`).
- **COLLISION.** An `o` square is one cover piece on its centre with the piece's own blocker (a piece without one gets a box of
  its own size): no more 7 m box round a small prop. Machine boxes are `block: true` on whole squares. A deck under the sky gets
  railings where it ends at a drop. A lever / an act on a deck is found by HEIGHT (`pdY`), not by the room's floor level.
- **The boards** were re-laid for it (street = two ferry plots, channel = ride one piece + call the other, door = ride the
  stairwell, connect = walk the four turning floors, rail = a lever at each stage, worlds = marbles at the start + the junction's
  levers further on, escort = the bell at the start + the hub's lever further on). `node bake-dungeons.js` searches levers only.
- **Proven in the browser 11-15** (shots in /mnt/project-files/dungeons/proof2/): all ten start to exit on foot, with stretches
  on the skateboard across seams (crypt, street, channel, connect, rail, root).
- Still stand-in: fights, the Procession's guardian, flat Three Little Worlds, no drawn water, no decor pass. There is no UNDO /
  RESET in the world: START OVER on the level list (or `PD.reset()`).

**Civic Center, THE INTERIORS (2026-11-13/15, mondo 21:04 "let's go ahead and do the interiors", his OK on the floor plans 21:21):**
nine walk-ins furnished in place in the city room, all in `docs/disaster-city/districts/C.js` "THE INTERIORS": Fire Station (8 x 8

## DISASTER CITY, THE INTERIOR POLISH (2026-11-15, mondo: "rugs/carpets flickering, desks clipping through chairs, zombie floating in the air ... do another polish pass on disaster city"; 09:07 "chairs and a chandelier and stuff floating in the air ... a building by the recording studio")
One pass over every walk-in (99 hollow texbuildings) of `site_prebuilt_downtown_streets`, whichever district wrote it. It lives in the BAKE, so a later district edit cannot bring a fault back:
`docs/disaster-city/interior-polish.js`, run by `node bake-disaster-city.js` after the prop pass (`DC_NO_POLISH=1` = the room as the district files wrote it; `DC_POLISH_LOG=1` prints what it could not mend). It MOVES rows, it never drops one. The tally is the bake's `interiorPolish` line.
- **The facts it is built on** (three-renderer.js): a walk-in draws its own floor at +0.03 m, its inside walls 0.30 m in from the row's edge, its ceiling at H − 0.32. A prop WITHOUT `floor: true` stands on `hqTerrainFeet` = the TOP of the wall / ghost block beside it (so on the roof); `y` under 1 m is a lift, 1 m and over a height (the bake adds the ground). The HQ camera's near plane makes two faces under 3 mm apart flicker; 6 mm is safe.
- **1 The roof standers**: every prop of a walk-in gets `floor: true` (543 rows; 97 were drawn on roofs in Financial + Hero Plaza), bar one on a low block on purpose (a till on a counter block) and vehicles.
- **2 The shared surfaces**: the renderer's own `_hqArchGeometry` is run on every arch part; two same-facing faces within 3 mm and overlapping move 6 mm apart (the smaller one; the room's floor, walls, ceiling never move). 90 floor + 249 wall pairs; 16 cyl/roof shapes cannot be pushed (same material, left).
- **3 The rugs**: a `lay` / rug / carpet / doormat prop is lifted 12 mm over the highest floor layer under it (a round rug's top was at 0.029 m under the floor's 0.030 m: the flicker). **4 The sunk props**: a prop under a raised floor layer is lifted onto it.
- **5 The buried linings**: a lining nearer the row's edge than 0.30 m is behind the room's wall (Civic's 0.17 m, Financial's 0.27 m): per wall they come out to 0.33 m with everything in front of them and the props on that wall.
- **6 The clipping props**, from the measured model sizes (`docs/disaster-city/prop-sizes.json`, written by `node docs/disaster-city/measure-props.js`: two range requests a GLB, 429 models; RERUN IT after adding models to an interior, an unmeasured key is left alone): a piece over the ceiling comes down / is made the room's height; a piece in the wall comes in to its face (a hung piece lying across its wall is turned flat; a neighbour it then stands in comes with it); two pieces in each other step apart (the lighter one, never a blocker; a chair may stand 15 cm under its table; a spell's guitar on a wall is 1 m, not 2.66 m).
- **The desk through the chair**: `school_desk` (proc) draws ITS OWN blue chair 0.56 m out of its front; a district that also set a chair there had two in one spot. The pass counts the desk's chair as a piece.
- **By hand, in the district files**: E.js `putProp` added the ground twice (the tool adds it): the concert hall's orchestra, the drum kits, the wedding cakes hung 12 m up, over the dome (his 09:07 screenshots). I.js + C.js dining tables were `round_table` = Camelot's 5.2 m Round Table: now `tulip_table`. C.js fire trucks 7.4 m (stood in each other), I.js the jet nose along its hangar (span 14), missiles along their cradles, F-inside.js the Bankers' mini fridge on its counter, U.js the library's shelf row out of the side walls.
- data.js `hqCityGrid` beds: a bed's `y` under 1 m is a lift (it read it as a height: a bed lifted 6 cm put its sleeper 5 m under the floor).
- three-renderer.js `ThreeRenderer.hq.dev.residents(race)`: a probe's read of the residents (where by the clock, body, asleep, clips).
- **The Zombie in the air** (fixed, PR after #1408): a resident given its body while already ASLEEP (the Zombie sleeps 8:00 to 18:00, so the officer always finds it in bed) took its height from `_hqNavQuery` at the bed = the walker's feet there = the top of the bed's ghost block or of the wall beside it (1 to 3 m up at 39 of the 55 beds; a headless check of `hqTerrainFeet` against `hqTerrainHeight` at every bed). three-renderer.js `_hqTickResidents`: a sleeper's floor is the room's ground at the bed (`hqTerrainHeight`). Not seen on screen: in the cloud browser a resident's model stays `loading` (the background lane never lands it).
- Scratch audit after: no floor flicker left, no prop on a roof, the hand worklist 175 down to 24 (the rest are approximations of procedural pieces).
### PLOT DUNGEONS, THE THIRD PASS (2026-11-15, mondo: "what is up with that lever? It looks nothing like a lever and there are 10 of them in a row ... Make a new lever. Do another pass on all the dungeons, visually and aesthetically")
- THE LEVER: `pd_lever` (catalogue, R2 `Assets/world/props/meshy/pd_lever.glb`, Meshy concept -> image-to-3d, originals + concept in project
  files `dungeons/meshy/`): ONE iron floor lever (pedestal, notched quadrant, red-gripped arm), 1.6 m. The Meshy mesh was split offline
  into two nodes (`pd_lever_base`, `pd_lever_arm`; the arm's origin is the hub) so the arm can swing: three-renderer.js `_hqPdPull`
  (`hq.pd.pull(counterId)`, the lever prop row carries `pd: { lever: <counter id> }`) throws it about z to the other end of the quadrant
  (0 <-> -0.84 rad, 0.42 s); map.js `_pdAct` throws the arm, waits 460 ms (`_pd.pulling`), then starts the move. `hq.pd.levers()` = dev read
  of the arms. The lever stands on a dark plate in a lit frame of the moved plot's colour (the post + cube lamp is gone); its blocker is
  0.9 m. `signal_lever_frame` (the twelve-lever frame) is no longer used by a dungeon (it stays in the Industrial rail room).
- THE DRESSING (data.js `PD_DRESS` + `pdDress`, called by `pdRoomDef`): every look dresses its plots by itself from the cells, seeded by
  level + plot (the same plot always wears the same things; a new level is dressed the day it is written). Per look: `hang` (wall pieces on
  the wall beside a floor square), `big` (a whole-square blocker centred on a wall square of a room 3+ deep, never in a doorway lane
  (squares 5-6), never beside a stair, never two touching, even by a corner; each gets a 2.9 m ghost blocker `big<x>_<y>`), `stand` (small
  floor decor against a wall), `corner`, `litter`, `tops` (an open look's blocks: the street's trees and planters), `field` (a plot with no
  door at all, a machine's own ground, is strewn all over). Rows are [key, weight, { h | span, y, in, rot }]. Dressing never stands within
  1.6 squares of a mark or on a trace, never on the plot's edge. Dressing props wear `noBlock`, `noLight`, `mesh: false`, `scatter`
  (new row flags `noBlock` / `noLight` in three-renderer.js `_hqPlaceProps`): decor never blocks and never takes one of the level's 11
  lights (a torch keeps its glow). A plot row may wear `dress: false` or its own table. `node bake-dungeons.js` fails a level when a big
  piece cuts a plot's floor in two.
- THE WIDE VIEW reads now: a closed look's solid mass wears a dark cap over its top (draw rows `top<i>`, grown over the walls' own
  thickness) and dark skirts on the plot's outer sides (`skirt_<side><i>`), so from above only the rooms are lit.
- THE DRAWN PIECES: a `lamp` mark is a signal lantern (foot, post, caged head, cap); a `stand` / `take` stands on a pedestal (foot, shaft
  in the look's trim, cap); Two to Open's battery is the `steam_turbine` on a lit plinth and its locks are two `retro_control_panel`s on a
  plinth under their lantern (ghost blockers keep the old sizes); Three Little Worlds' machines are stone (`bricks_3`).
- THE WORKS LOOK (Traveling Door, Two to Open): the stained drywall is gone, the walls are `urban:MetalCorrugatedPainted3a`.
- Still stand-in: the fights, the Procession's guardian, no drawn water in Missing Channel, Three Little Worlds is flat.

## DISASTER CITY, THE MOLE'S RIM (2026-11-15, mondo: "theres still this wall or raised curve by the light house")
- What it was: a rim of ground 5.25 m high and one height sample (0.875 m) thick along z = 84, x 252 to 311: the whole north side of
  the breakwater. NOT a kerb stone (PR #1336), not the sea wall, not the canal (PR #1402).
- Why: districts/B.js `beach()` cuts the beach strip flat to level 0 from z = Z0 south, and the bay north of Bayside deep from z = Z0
  north. A `sink` plateau cuts only strictly inside its rectangle (data.js hqTerrainCompile: `din <= 0` skips), so on the shared line
  z = Z0 neither one cut and the city's level there (P11-07, level 3) stayed standing. The height grid has a sample row exactly on 84.
- Fix: the level-0 cut starts half a metre north of Z0, so the two overlap. One row of the bake changed.
- RULE: two `sink` rectangles that share an edge must OVERLAP, never just touch. Check offline: sample hqTerrainHeight over the whole
  field and list samples more than 1 m above both neighbours; after the fix only stairs / ramps (roof flights, the overpass stair, the
  parking deck ramp) are left.

building's walls ('I' square: the hotel lobby, the Private garden's own beds) is the district's indoor planting, left alone. The bake

## DISASTER CITY, THE EXTERIOR POLISH (2026-11-15, mondo: "do an exterior pass too on disaster city ... Bench clipping through a wall or curb, probably from the elevation pass. Make sure any generated shapes for buildings and stuff have a texture/material")
One pass over every OUTDOOR prop of `site_prebuilt_downtown_streets` + the bare generated shapes. It lives in the BAKE (`docs/disaster-city/exterior-polish.js`, run by `node bake-disaster-city.js` after every other pass; `DC_NO_EXT=1` skips it, `DC_EXT_LOG=1` lists every row it touched), so a later district edit cannot bring a fault back. It MOVES rows and sets `floor`; it never drops one. NOT SEEN ON SCREEN (RULE #1c): checked offline against the compiled room.
- **Why the prop check missed them**: props.js reads the ground from the tool's own squares (`LV.at`). The game stands a prop on the COMPILED ground. So the bake now writes the room to a scratch copy of data.js, loads it headless (load-data.js `file`), compiles it (`hqTerrainInfo`, about 8 s) and hands the real `hqTerrainHeight` / `hqTerrainFeet` to the pass, then writes the props again.
- **1 THE WALL STANDERS (104)**: three-renderer.js `_hqPlaceProps` stands a prop on `hqTerrainFeet` at its middle; within a body's reach (0.34 m) of a wall that is the wall's TOP. Every vent / utility box / pay phone / cabinet set flush on a building (93), and a bench, 3 planters, 2 vending machines, 2 road signs, a pot, a crate, boxes stood 1 to 11 m up on the wall beside them. Each gets `floor: true` (the ground under it). The same fault indoors was THE INTERIOR POLISH's roof standers.
- **2 THE STEP STRADDLERS (125 moved)**: a step of THE LEVELS is drawn about 0.9 m wide, mostly on the LOW side of the plot line. A bench set against a fence on that line (0.75 m off it) stood half way up the bank (his screenshot): 57 benches, 14 cones, 10 planters, 9 bins, 6 dumpsters, 4 barricades, bags, barrels, crates, a bus, a taxi. Flat = the least-squares plane through the ground under the whole real footprint fits within 7 cm and is no steeper than 22 % (a street's slope passes, a step / bank / kerb lip does not). A faulty row moves to the nearest flat, clear spot by the placement rules: a thing that blocks to a whole square's middle, decor off the middle, a car along its street (5 m at most), a wall thing along its wall. 12 wall things whose wall runs along a bank the whole way keep the wall and hang at the bank's top (`y` = the lift).
- **3 THE LEFT OUT (14)**: props.js `check` dropped a shared prop with no clear spot in its short reach; it returns them now (`dropped`) and the pass puts each back at the nearest clear flat spot (a wall thing with no wall stands free). `left_out` in the check's tally is no longer a loss.
- **props.js FIXED**: `^city_` (the pack buildings) also matched `city_bench` / `city_bin`, so no city bench or bin was ever checked. Fixed (`^city_(?!bench$|bin$)`): the check now moves 16 of them out of walls / doorways.
- **Left alone on purpose**: props on a deck / footbridge / landing, afloat, hung at a height, indoors, the landmarks, palms (THE TREES STAND IN SOIL owns their bed), the Collapse's rubble on its mound (`hill`). One taxi under Financial's Taxi court canopy has a 0.38 m lip under one side and no clear spot within a car length: listed (`stuck`).
- F.js: the Service garage's SUV stood at 20 degrees in the 3.5 m lane, its tail in the terrace's wall (and was drawn on that wall's top): along the lane now.
- **THE BANKS WEAR THE WALL** (three-renderer.js `_hqTerrainMat` + `_ewNodeTerrain`, both renderers): the painted ground sheets are laid from above only, so a bank between two plots (up to 7 m) wore its yard's grass / paving as streaks stretched straight down (the "tall grass wall" in his screenshot). In a room whose ground is `terrain.slope` and painted, a steep face (the sharpened up-weight under 0.25 to 0.6) wears the room's CLIFF sheet (the city: `urban:ConcreteStriped2a`, a concrete retaining wall), read on the face's own axis. Streets, ramps and stair flights are too flat to count. `window.EW_NO_STEEP_CLIFF` = off.
- **THE BARE PARTS WEAR A SURFACE** (three-renderer.js `_hqBuildArchRows` matOf, `HQ_ARCH_SURFACE`, `_hqArchSurface`): an arch part with no `key` was one flat Phong colour: 8,057 parts of the city (5,594 outdoors: frames, trims, awnings, plinths, posts; 2,463 indoors: counters, shelves, legs). The renderer reads the part's colour as a material and gives it that sheet, colour kept (the sheet's average is divided out): dark greys = plate steel `calm_rivets`, mid greys = `calm_concrete`, browns = `calm_planks`, everything else = painted plaster `urban:PlasterWallPainted1a`. Lit parts (`glow`), glass and decals stay. No data change, so every district's later parts get it too. The ladders' steel and the fire escapes' iron decks (`_hqBuildClimbs`) wear the plate sheet as well. `window.EW_ARCH_BARE = true` = the flat colours back.
- All four sheets were on R2 and in use already: no new art, none of his textures touched, no gold.

  F cool white / FINANCIAL bank green, U ivory / UNIVERSITY maroon, H bright warm white / HERO PLAZA red, E pink / ENTERTAINMENT purple,
  I deep orange / INDUSTRIAL hazard yellow (dark ink), S stadium white / SPORTS + CULTURE green, B aqua / BAYSIDE teal.

- data.js compile: `info.lampLooks` = gen.looks, `info.lamps[]` keep `d` / `b`.

## CAMELOT, THE DISTRICT FILES — one thread a district (2026-11-16)

mondo 11-16: "every single zone needs to be like that. now. so we can work in parallel" (like Disaster City's district files). A set-up
change: how the zone is WRITTEN, not what is built. The baked room `site_prebuilt_camelot_kingdom` is byte for byte the same before and
after (data.js sha256 `fc5334b0…` both times; `node bake-camelot.js` on fresh main, then again after the split, `cmp` clean; done twice, the
second time on top of the castle thread's banner / stair / tilt changes that merged meanwhile).

- **The files** (`docs/areas/camelot/districts/`, loaded by `bake-camelot.js` through ONE hook, "THE DISTRICT FILES" in the tool):
  | File | District | Plots | Holds |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `K.js` | The Castle | 8 | the castle's OUTSIDE on the kingdom's plots: Keep, wings, towers, Stables, Armoury, the hill's drums and cheek walls, the Lists, the courts, the four doors into the palace room (was `buildCastle()`) |
  | `T.js` | The Village | 28 | Chapel, Smithy, Inn + their insides, the market, graveyard, green, gates' dressing |
  | `T-houses.js` | The Village | (same) | the 43 houses: `frontOf()`, `houseKind()`, `houseLook()` (the five kinds). Called by T.js, not by the tool |
  | `L.js` | The Looking-Glass Garden | 6 | the drawn hedges, chessboard, courts, caterpillar, tea party |
  | `F.js` | The Fairy Forest | 6 | pond, ring, spring, knolls |
  | `N.js` | The Snowy Pines | 8 | sleigh, snowmen, campfires, the yeti |
  | `W.js` | The Forest | 8 | the glades' knolls, logs, ferns |
  Each file's header is its thread's brief: its plots, what stands there, what is missing or waits mondo, the hooks.
- **Why the Village has two files**: the houses are most of the village's code and a job of their own (43 looks today, insides later), and
  the street dressing never touches them. T.js calls T-houses.js at the one place the houses are written, so two threads can hold one each.
- **The hook**: a file exports `first(ctx)` (right after the hill, before the moat and the wall: K uses it, so the castle's rows still lead
  the room) and / or `build(ctx)` (after every shared piece stands). The tool runs them in a FIXED order, K T (the road in from the bay)
  L F N W, not by file name: the order rows are written is the order they are baked, and every scattered piece (`dec`) draws from one
  stream of dice, so a district that adds a `dec` moves the scatter of every district after it (a few decimetres, harmless, but it shows
  in the diff of the baked block). ctx is listed in the tool's hook comment.
- **What stayed in the tool (shared, nobody's district)**: the plan's reading (`layout.json` cells, plots, the houses' and walk-ins' squares),
  the kit (`sheet()`, `royalBanner()`, `building()`, `inside()`, `solid()`, `flushArch()`), THE HILL (`tier` / `flight` / `parapets`: the two stone steps and
  the three stairs), the moat and the bridges, the town wall with its towers and gates, the ways out (`oldgarden`, `deadtree`, the bay and
  its two braziers and signpost, THE MIRROR's door on L's plot P00-04, the links' ends), the open ground, the paint, the tree zones, the
  checks, the shell and sky, the room's text.

### The rules for a district thread
1. **One thread = one district file.** Take its row on the board (docs/notes/claims.md) in your first PR; free it in your last.
2. **Never edit** `bake-camelot.js`, `layout.json`, another district's file or the baked block by hand. A change to the tool or a shared
   piece (a kit helper, the hill, the wall, the moat, a road, a way out, the paint, the sky) needs the tool's row taken on the board first,
   with a dated note saying what changes; keep such a PR small and separate from district work. The plan's squares (where a building or a
   hedge stands, what is open ground) are `layout.json`: the tool's.
3. **The castle's inside** (`site_prebuilt_camelot_palace`, `bake-camelot-castle.js`) and `districts/K.js` are the castle thread's.
4. **Scope of a district thread**: exteriors, interiors, dressing, atmosphere, polish, on its own plots, with its own row ids (`cam:` + a
   name no other district uses). Visual work gets a browser run (RULE #1c): `node playtest_city.js site_prebuilt_camelot_kingdom '[views]'`.
5. **Rebake and merge**: `node bake-camelot.js` (1 s), `node --check data.js`, commit your file AND data.js, bump the `?v=` token (data.js is
   an R2 file), PR, merge, `node sync-zip.js --upload`.
6. **When another district landed first** (the baked block conflicts in data.js): `git fetch origin main && git merge origin/main`, resolve
   every file EXCEPT the block by hand keeping both sides, then throw the conflicted block away and rerun `node bake-camelot.js` (it
   rewrites everything between `CAMELOT-KINGDOM-BEGIN / END` from the merged files). Never keep one side of the baked block wholesale,
   never hand-merge inside it. Merge main again right before you merge your PR, and rebake if anything under `docs/areas/camelot/` or the
   tool came in.
7. The tool's checks are everybody's: a piece on a square that is not free ground, a prop not in the catalogue, a plot not walked to from
   the bay, stops the bake. Fix your file; do not loosen the check.
- **Where older notes point now**: "bake-camelot.js `buildCastle()`" = `districts/K.js` + the tool's THE HILL; "bake-camelot.js `houseKind()` /
  `houseLook()`" = `districts/T-houses.js`; `sheet().roof` and the other kit pieces are still in the tool.

## CAMELOT CASTLE, ONE STACKED BUILDING — the palace's own room, six levels (2026-11-15)
mondo on the next-pieces picture: "can we make the 3 rooms stacked like part of the same building, but the castle can be its own loading
screen" + "real architecture/floor plan"; on the floor plans (`docs/plans/camelot/camelot_castle_stacked_plan.png`): "1) yes", "lets not worry
about the sky castle for now, and no it would not be in the same room", "do all 3 floors, not just 2", the five house kinds "are fine".
- **The room** `site_prebuilt_camelot_palace` (site `prebuilt_camelot`, part `palace`), written by `node bake-camelot-castle.js` between
  `CAMELOT-PALACE-BEGIN / END` in data.js (never hand-edit). 30 x 12 squares = the palace's own footprint (wings u 0-8 and 22-30, the Keep
  8-22). The tool carries the Desert insides' kit (`mk`, bake-desert-insides.js) and its walk check.
- **SIX LEVELS, 7 m apart**: Undercroft 0 · floor 0 at 7 (every way out) · floor 1 at 14 · floor 2 at 21 · floor 3 at 28 · Battlements 35.
  - Undercroft: Merlin's Workshop with the Orb under the throne, Gaoler's Room, three cells, antechamber, Crypt of Kings, Ossuary, Sally
    Port passage, Well Chamber, the Vaults (under the Kitchen), the Cistern (under the Barracks).
  - Floor 0: the Throne Hall (14 m high), Robing Room, lobby, Chancery; Kitchen wing (Great Kitchen, Buttery, Pantry, Servery); Barracks wing
    (Barracks, Arms Store, Captain's Room, Guard Room).
  - Floor 1: the gallery round the hall's void, King's Office, Treasury, the Chapel Royal (west), the Knights' Hall (east).
  - Floor 2: Long Gallery, King's Solar, Presence Chamber, Queen's Chamber, Wardrobe, Nursery; the wings' roofs are walked on.
  - Floor 3: the Great Library, Merlin's Study, the War Room. Battlements: the roof walk, the bridge walk, the Spire Room (its sky door is
    drawn shut: the sky castle waits).
- **CHANGED FROM THE DRAWN PLAN, and why** (tell mondo): the plan drew the Great Stair as stacked flights in a stair hall. The engine holds one
  ground height a point, and a stair is ground, so no stair can stand over another or over a walked room. Built instead: ONE straight stair
  east along the Keep's north wall (floor 0 > 1 > 2 > 3, a landing a floor, rows v 0-1), the last flight back west up to the Battlements, and
  the two ways to the cellar as cellar stairs in the wings (Servery > Vaults, Guard Room > Cistern). The north range's rooms are one square
  shallower for it. The plan's Undercroft Hall and tunnel became the Sally Port passage and the Well Chamber (the portal's sill is solid
  ground between them). The Spire Room is in the Spire's foot on the Battlements (no climb inside the Spire).
- **THE RULES THIS BUILD FOUND (stacked floors; they hold for any room):**
  1. The field = the lowest floor. A floor over a walked room is a `bridge` slab; where nothing lies under it, make it solid (`plateau`),
     and put every way out there: a wall door's sill and a free door's pad are read on the FIELD.
  2. Slabs overlap each other and solid ground by 0.5 m (a slab is read 0.12 m in from its edge; a bare seam is a crack).
  3. A flight ARRIVES 0.4 m into its landing (the landing slab starts exactly on the flight's last line) and LEAVES from 0.5 m under the
     landing it starts on. `edge: 0` on the ramp.
  4. A wall with `y0` only HANGS (lets the floor below walk under it) when its foot is over the highest ground under the WHOLE piece.
     A piece that runs on over a stair stands from the ground up and shuts the floors below: cut the wall where each flight starts and
     ends, and where a flight's 0.4 / 0.5 m run-on lies (`V1` in the tool).
  5. A prop or a native on a floor carries `y` = the floor's height (under 1 it stands on the field, in the cellar). The kit's
     blocker / doorway check is kept a floor (`R.lvl`).

covers every later rebuilt area too (the Woods on plots had the same fault).

## THE WOODS, THE DISTRICT FILES (2026-11-16, mondo: "every single zone needs to be like that. now. so we can work in parallel")
The Woods is written the way Disaster City is: the tool holds what is shared, each district's content is its own file, and one thread per
district can work at the same time. A set-up change only: the baked room did not change (see THE PROOF).
- **The files**: `docs/areas/woods/districts/C.js` (The Clearing, plots x 0..2 · y 3..5), `T.js` (The Redwood Trail, x 0..2 · y 0..2), `G.js` (The Ritual
  Ground, x 3..5 · y 0..2), `M.js` (Dead Man's Cave, x 3..5 · y 3..5). Each starts with its brief: its nine plots, what stands there today, what is
  missing or waits for mondo, the hooks. Read your file's header before anything else.
- **The one hook** (bake-woods.js "THE DISTRICT FILES", right after the seeded roll): a file exports any of `tailor(ctx)` (its own changes to the plan's
  squares, before the levels), `dress(ctx)` / `horror(ctx)` / `life(ctx)` (the three passes as they were built), `build(ctx)` (new work, after the three),
  `wood` (the feature trees in its forest mass), `treeZones(ctx)` / `airZones(ctx)` (its boxes of `terrain.gen.zones` and `shell.atmos.zones`). The passes
  run C, T, G, M; the zone boxes are written T, G, C, M (the mountain row and the Snowline's snow come first: the first box wins).
- **What stays in the tool (shared)**: the plan (layout.json), THE TRAILS AND THE PATHS, the ways out (every door row, the `LINK_ENDS`, the Camelot
  spur check), the glades, the levels, the open ground and its paint, the creek + the three pools + the decks, the helpers (put / dec / tree / native /
  hput / hdec / life / fly / sow), the room-wide fern / stump / log scatter, the `FULL` tree map, the checks, the room's text and shell. The trees
  themselves (bake-trees.py, `rt:*_full`, tree kinds) are the trees row on the board. The air's engine (three-renderer.js `_hqBuildAtmos`) is engine code.
- **THE DICE AS THEY FELL**: the room is thrown with one stream of dice. Each district's pass, and the forest's feature trees, now starts on the dice
  it had on the day of the split (the tool's `DICE` table), so a district that adds or drops a roll never moves another district's pieces. `tailor` and
  `build` start on the district's own number. Two things still reach across: (1) a `sow` row's seed is the count of feature rows before it, so a feature
  row added inside an OLD pass re-throws every later scatter in the room: put new feature rows in `build`; (2) a `tailor` that changes squares moves
  the forest's feature trees and the open-ground rows after it (the same dice, other squares). Both show up in the bake's diff, neither breaks anything.
- **The guard**: a helper asked for another district's plot throws (`not yours: districts/T.js asked for P03-02 …`). Rows pushed by hand (`features.push`,
  `props.push`) are not checked: keep them on your own nine plots.

**THE RULES FOR A DISTRICT THREAD**
1. One thread = one district file. Take your district's row on the board (docs/notes/claims.md) in your first PR; free it in your last.
2. The scope of a district thread: exteriors, interiors, dressing, atmosphere, polish, on its own nine plots. Edit only your `districts/<LETTER>.js`
   (+ your notes here, + a catalogue row in data.js for a new prop, + MODEL_LIST.md when a model is added).
3. Nobody edits bake-woods.js, layout.json or a shared piece (a door, a link end, a trail, the water, the levels, the sky, the helpers) without a dated
   note on the board first, signed with the side. Need a new helper or a hook? Ask there; the holder of the "tool + shared pieces" row adds it.
   Never edit another district's file. The trees (kinds, crowns) are closed by mondo ("Good, keep them") and belong to the trees row.
4. Never hand-edit data.js between `WOODS36-BEGIN` / `WOODS36-END`. Bake: `node bake-woods.js` (`--dry-run` = the counts only; `WOODS_DUMP=1` prints
   the square map). The tool checks every prop key against the catalogue, every native against the unit list, and that all 36 plots are reached on foot.
5. **When another district landed first**: `git fetch origin main && git merge origin/main`. A conflict inside the baked block is NEVER solved by keeping
   one side: take either side of the block to get past the conflict, run `node bake-woods.js`, and commit what the tool wrote (it holds both districts,
   because both district files merged cleanly). A conflict in your own district file: keep both sides by hand. Merge main and rebake again right before
   you merge the PR.
6. data.js is an R2 file: a PR that changes the baked room bumps the `?v=` token in index.html and runs `node sync-zip.js --upload` (RULE #1, #1b).
   A visual change gets a browser run through probe-fast.js (RULE #1c); in this room use `"fp": true` on open ground and `--flags=EW_PERF_LOW`.
7. What mondo has said that binds every district: no doors in the Woods (ways are trails); no unexplained dead ends; no procedural stand-ins shown to
   him; no apple tree (a Meshy tree); every new glow carries `noLight`; the cabin has no game role yet; small things only on a path's edge, nothing on a path.

**THE PROOF OF NO CHANGE (11-16)**: on main at b055c5b the old tool was run (`node bake-woods.js`: data.js unchanged, sha256 9afc5d47), the tool was split,
and the split tool was run: data.js is byte for byte the same file (sha256 9afc5d47, 118,860 bytes of room, the same counts: 361 props, 377 feature rows,
6 doors, 17 natives). No difference to list, so no browser run, no token bump and nothing to upload.

  the Observatory wears `marble_light` (the stucco sheet read brown). PROBE LESSON: `dev.teleport` puts the walker at height 0; in a room whose ground is not
  at 0 pass `y` = the ground there (hqTerrainCompile(room).hFn(x, z)), or the camera sits under the land and photographs the sea sheet from below.
- **Not done / to know**:

  from Bayside or from the Cove. From the Hills you do not see the city below (the south edge is plain dry land: rooms are separate). The Shasta trail's
  door still opens at the Woods' Snowline (the Woods are not changed). The city's closed VATICAN GATE is untouched (ask mondo when the Vatican is built).

## THE MOUNTAINS, THE DISTRICT FILES — one thread a district (2026-11-16, second side; mondo: set the Mountains up like Disaster City's districts)

A set-up change: how the zone is written, not what is built. Everything that stands on the plots moved out of `bake-mountains.js` into six files,
`docs/areas/mountains/districts/<LETTER>.js` (the letters are `layout.json` `districts`):

| File | District | Plots | Room |
|---|---|---|---|
| `N.js` | The North Pole village | 16 (P00..P03 x 00..03) | `site_prebuilt_northpole_plots` |
| `P.js` | The Snowy Pass | 12 (P04..P06 x 00..03) | `site_prebuilt_shasta_mountains` |
| `K.js` | The Ski Lodge + slopes | 12 (P07..P09 x 00..03) | same |
| `O.js` | Mount Olympus | 12 (P10..P12 x 00..03) | same |
| `S.js` | Mount Shasta | 20 (P13..P15 x 00..03, P13..P14 x 04..07) | same |
| (`H.js`) | The Hollywood Hills | 39 (H00..H12 x 00..02) | MOVED 11-16: Disaster City's district N, `docs/disaster-city/districts/N.js` ("THE HOLLYWOOD HILLS ARE PART OF DISASTER CITY") |

Each file's header is its thread's brief: its plots, what stands there, what is known missing or wrong, the shared pieces that stand in it, the hooks.

**The hook** (bake-mountains.js "THE DISTRICT FILES", the city's pattern): a file exports any of `tailor(t)` (change a square of its own plots before
the trails are cut), `apply(ctx)` (the standing things: walked-in buildings), `build(ctx)` (the dressing). A room runs its files in its `files` order
(Mountains: P, K, S, O), one stage for all, then the next. ctx = the room's helpers (put, dec, tree, native, building, look, feat, flat, S, gx/gz/mx/mz,
props, doors, marks ...) + `anchor(name, at)` + `say(old, race)` (an old room's native line) + `cabin` + the texture constants.
Two guards: while a file runs, `S()` throws on a plot of another district; `ctx.rnd` is that district's own random stream (room opt `streams`), so a
piece added in one district never moves another district's decor.

**THE RULES FOR A DISTRICT THREAD**
1. One thread = one district = one file. Take the district's row on the board (docs/notes/claims.md) in your first PR; free it in your last.
2. You edit YOUR district file only. Never another district's file. `data.js` between `MOUNTAINS-BEGIN` / `MOUNTAINS-END` is written by the tool: never by hand.
3. **The tool and the shared pieces belong to nobody's district.** `bake-mountains.js`, `docs/areas/mountains/layout.json` (the plan's squares, levels,
   names), the heights, the paint, the tree zones, the sky and edges, the spawn, every way out (wall doors, the links' ends, DOOR HQ's bay doors) and
   `ctx.cabin`: nobody changes them without a dated note in the board's Notes saying what and why, in the same PR. Keep such a change small and of use
   to every district (a new ctx helper, a new hook); a change to one district's look goes in its file. A plot's squares: use `tailor()`, not layout.json.
4. A district's own doors (a `wall: 'free'` door on its own plots, like the chairlift's pair) and its anchors are its own. The five anchors the tool
   needs must stay set: N `hearth`; O `painting`, `bayOlympus`; S `lemuria`, `bayShasta` (the tool throws when one is missing).
5. **Rebake and merge.** After an edit: `node --check` your file, `node bake-mountains.js` (1 s; it throws on a piece in the rock, on a taken square, on
   another district's plot, on a plot not reached on foot, on a step too steep). Before merging: `git fetch origin main && git merge origin/main`. If
   another district landed first, `data.js` conflicts inside the MOUNTAINS block: NEVER keep one side of the block wholesale and never merge it by hand.
   Take either side to clear the conflict (`git checkout --theirs data.js` is fine ONLY when the block is the file's one conflict; else resolve the
   other hunks by hand first), then run `node bake-mountains.js`: the tool rewrites the block from all six files as they stand after the merge. Check
   `git diff origin/main -- data.js` shows only the rows of your district. Same for the `?v=` token: merge, then re-bump (RULE #1b).
6. Scope of a district thread: exteriors, interiors, dressing, atmosphere, polish of its own plots. Not in scope without mondo: new game rules,
   characters, names or story (owner-rules.md), encounter tables (his baked tables), the Ice Wall, new ways between zones.
7. Visual work gets a probe run and pictures (RULE #1c / #1d, `probe-fast.js`). `dev.teleport` puts the walker at height 0: pass `y` = the ground there
   (`hqTerrainCompile(room).hFn(x, z)`), or the camera sits under the land. `MTN_DUMP=mtn|pole|hills node bake-mountains.js --dry-run` prints a room's walked map.
8. The Hills thread (H): that room's ground is Disaster City's north skyline, read at load, and the city draws its far sign where the twelve
   letters stand (`docs/disaster-city/districts/E.js` `edges.sign`). Moving the letters or the ground under them needs a note for the city's holder.
   The city's north beach (`districts/B.js` beach(), `bake-disaster-city.js` EDGES.n.cap) is the city's, not the Hills'.

**PROOF OF NO CHANGE** (rebake before and after, both loaded with load-data.js and compared room by room, 255 rooms): the North Pole room and the Hills
room are the same to the byte; every link end and bay door is the same; in the Mountains room the heights, the paint, the tree zones, the doors, the
natives and the marks are the same, and the feature and prop lists hold the same rows in another ORDER, one cause: the Warming Hut (district P) is now
written before the Lodge and the Rental Hut (district K), because P runs first (its `texbuilding` row #228 -> #226, its `arch` row #285 -> #283, its 8
props ahead of the Lodge's and the Rental Hut's 41). No row changed. The block's first comment line names the district files. No browser run (a no-change refactor).

## THE MOUNTAINS, THE ZONE KIT — what the pilot district learned, for the five district threads that follow (2026-11-16, district N thread)

mondo 11-16: "start one district thread in each to try to get it up to par with disaster city, so it will be easier to do the other districts once
that first district is fleshed out and knows what shared assets it can use for the zone". The North Pole village (N.js) is the Mountains' pilot.
Everything below was seen on screen in `site_prebuilt_northpole_plots`. Copy from N.js; a helper all six want belongs in bake-mountains.js (board note first).

**1. LOOK FIRST. What the first look found (expect the same in P, K, O, S, H: none was seen before):**
- A pack BUILDING used as a prop (`xmas_house`, 16 copies) was wider than its squares, cut its neighbours and read as a suburb. Buildings are built
  (`ctx.building` + an `arch` look), never a house prop.
- Windows = the glass sheet under a warm tint read OLIVE. A lit window is a `marble_light` box, tint 0xffc070, `glow` 1.0, with a white frame (N.js `pane`).
- Wall paint on the board sheet (`WD`) reads near BLACK at night: add `gain` 1.7 to the shell's two parts (`a.P.slice(-2)`) and to the gable (`tintEnd`).
- A board on a gable-front house must hang at z `d/2 + 0.86` or the gable's overhang hides it. Fonts: `fell` for the village; pick ONE per district.
- Black `ocean_rock` on snow looks wrong. Grey rock = `hw_stone*`, `psxg_rock_*`, `cave_stone`, or a `rocks_5` part.
- A plot's `B` run the walker cannot reach is counted in `unreachedSquares`: open it with `tailor`, do not leave it.
- The probe: `dev.teleport` needs `y` = the ground (the village: 1.75, the lake + roads 0). A view from `fp: true` INSIDE a roof or wall shows nonsense.

**2. INSIDES (true for every walked-in `texbuilding` in a plot room):**
- The building's own inside takes NO light: at night a furnished room is black. N.js `lit(a, w, h, d, dr, key, tint, glow, ctx)` lines the walls, floor
  and ceiling with thin boxes 0.30 m in, `glow` 0.85 + `gain` 1.7 (a part with `glow` is drawn UNLIT at tint x glow: 0.25 is DARKER than none). The city
  does the same with quads (`kind: 'wall'`, each turned to its wall: F-atmos.js `coat`); a quad not turned to its wall does not show.
- Every inside prop gets `floor: true` (N.js `onFloor(B)` wraps `B.put`): without it a prop within a body's reach of a wall stands on the wall's TOP.
- A prop's `y`: under 1 = a lift; from 1 up = a height from the ROOM's floor, so add the plot's ground (N.js `UP(h)`). A hung piece: `mount: 0` + `UP(h)`.
- Fire: catalogue `hearth_fire` (`w` / `h` in metres, a real light) in an OPEN brick hearth (N.js `hearth`). Outdoors: `campfire`, `brazier` (real lights).
- THE SQUARES (done in N, pass 6; the city's rule, F-inside.js): a thing that BLOCKS stands on the MIDDLE of a whole 3.5 m square; chairs, lamps, sacks,
  side tables stand off the middles; wall pieces take no square. A plot building covers whole squares, so its squares' middles are (+-1.75, ...) in its
  own frame (N.js `SQ`, `at(h, 'BL', key)`). A 2 x 2 house takes TWO blockers at most (the two back squares, or one back + one front on the same side):
  the door's square and one more, joined edge to edge, stay free. Check that no free square is shut in (a blocker on FR beside a blocked BL shuts BR in).
  An `arch` shape that should block (the coal heap) gets a ghost wall: `R.feat({ k: 'wall', ..., ghost: true, rail: false })`. Outdoors `fallen_log`
  and big crates block: `put`, not `dec`.

**3. THE KIT (all in the catalogue or the sheets today):**
- Walls: `WD` boards (painted with `gain`), log brown 0x7a5a40 (`ctx.cabin`, districts K and P), stone foot `rocks_5` 0xa8a8b0, snow roof `ice` 0xf4f8ff, chimney
  `bricks_2` 0xb86a54, trim `marble_light` 0xf6f6f2 (the wood sheets cannot be painted white), gilt = `gold`, coal / dark rock = `obsidian`.
- The village palette: red 0xb84438, green 0x3f6b4a, cream 0xd8c8a8, blue 0x5a7890, ginger 0x9a6238, plum 0x7a4a6a. Warm light 0xffb050 to 0xffc070 against
  the blue night is the zone's one rule of light; coloured bulbs (N.js `bulbs`) are the village's own.
- Signs: N.js `board()`; fonts by id from three-renderer.js `HQ_SIGN_FONTS` (`xmas`, `marc`, `pacifico`, `bangers`, `rye`, `stencil`, `fell` ...). People: export
  `encounters` from the district file (the tool writes the room's table); pick from the roster by `RACE_PROFILES[race].biomes`.
- Lamp post: N.js `lampPost` (candy stripes: the VILLAGE's; another district should keep the lantern and change the post). No lamp model exists.
- Winter props: `xmas_*` (trees, snowmen, gifts, wreaths, garlands, stockings, food), `sleigh`, `signpost`, `park_bench`, `ancient_well`, `fallen_log`,
  `stump`, `hw_straw`, `hw_fence`, `psx_wooden_crate_*`, `meshy_burlap_sack`, `cardboard_boxes`, `rabbit`, `crow`, `dog`, `brazier`, `campfire`.
- Inside: the PSX pack (`psx_bed_1`, `psx_dinner_table_1`, `psx_chair_mp_3`, `psx_sofa_1`, `psx_wardrobe_mp_1`, `psx_shelf_mp_*`, `psx_display_cabinet_mp_*`),
  `rocking_chair`, `rug_round`, `table_lamp`, `form_counter`, `cash_register`, `deck_oven`, `bread_rack`, `mailbox_bank`, `platform_scale`, `tool_pegboard`,
  `tool_chest`, `ships_bell`, `notice_board`, `wall_clock`. Dark pack furniture reads black: put it against a lit wall.

**FOR THE NEXT THREAD (learned here):**
- A free-standing `look` stands on the ground under its ORIGIN, not under each part: put the origin on a walked square of the plot (O.js `plotLook(id, tag, ox, oy, hug, fn)`),
  never on the plot's corner (a rock corner lifted the whole look out of sight). On a sloping plot set `hug: true` on the row (every corner then lies on the ground under it)
  and cut long beams into one piece a square.
- A plot is level only two squares either side of its middle row; the rest grades to its neighbours. Something that must stand level takes `R.flats.push([sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1, 'N'])`
  (the side names the edge whose height it keeps).
- A built shape that should block: one ghost wall on the square's middle (O.js `block`), and the square goes in `R.taken`.
- Marble under the room's light is grey without `gain`: 1.7 on `marble_light`, 1.6 on `gold`. `dev.teleport` with `fp: true` and a raised `y` is the only far view (the third-person camera stays close).
- A curved wall or tier = `cyl` with `arc`, `a0`, `ri` (angle 0 = east, 90 = south).

3. The seats and tiers block (ghost walls): nobody climbs them. The Stadium's track stays open end to end.

5. No names added: the plots keep the plan's names; no sign boards.
6. The Temple's statue is the wish list's `god_statue` since the model pass (it was Lady Justice).
10. Every brazier became a tripod bowl (the brief's word), so their real lights are gone; say so if you want some braziers back for the night.
7. The Temple has a wooden double door that swings (your rule for walk-ins); it was an open frame.
8. Six more units stand in the district (valkraye, giant, nephilim, unicorn, occulus, watcher): your word 11-16 was more NPCs; all are `divine` / `ancient` units. None has a line (no invented words).
9. The spyglass at the Goat Track is the game's modern telescope (the world is a parody of the real one).

**NEEDS A MODEL:** nothing open. PLACED in the model pass (11-16): olive tree, grape trellis, laurel wreath, chariot, discus and javelin rack, tripod bowl, Greek couch,

**6. ADDED BY THE SKI LODGE THREAD (district K, 2026-11-16):**
- THE MODEL LIST FIRST (mondo 11-16). Catalogue rows on R2 that fit a snow zone and that no Mountains file had used: `flood_mast` (a real night light, 26 m),
  `festoon`, `pa_speaker`, `ticket_booth`, `turnstile` / `metro_gate`, `rope_stanchion`, `surfboard_rack`, `scarf_rack`, `key_rack`, `brochure_rack`, `map_table`,
  `hw_fence` (a wooden fence, the Halloween pack), `item_police_barricade`, `traffic_barrel`, `telescope`, `radio_console`, `field_radio`, `arms_trophy`,
  `pinball_machine`, `psx_armchair_*` / `psx_sofa_*`, `psx_metal_barrel_mp_*`, `wrapped_pallet`, `hand_truck`, `wolf`, `eagle`, `quarter_pipe`, `riser_*`.
  Looked inside the Christmas pack's one file (`Christmas.dae`, 69 nodes): every piece has a row but `Snow` .. `Snow.005`, `Christmas_star`, `Ribbon`,
  two spare hats; the six `Snow*` are the snow caps of the pack's own house and trees, not loose drifts. Nothing ski-shaped is on R2 (no skis, snowboard,
  snow gun, groomer, snowmobile, netting): K.js header, NEEDS A MODEL.
- `hug: true` on an `arch` row lays every corner of every part on the ground under that corner. A box 24 m long is then a straight line from the ground
  at one end to the ground at the other, a fixed height over both: the lift's cables. `look()` does not pass it: set it on `ctx.ARCH[ctx.ARCH.length - 1]`.
  The ground it reads includes `ramp` rows (a kicker lifts whatever hangs over it): keep hugging parts' corners off ramps.
- A `ramp` row laid ALONG the fall line with `h0 = h1` lies on the slope (the compile adds the ground at each end), and its `edge` rounds BOTH flanks by a
  smoothstep: `w: 17.5, edge: 7, h 3.3` is a snow wall with a curved way up, a 3.5 m top and a back to roll down, in one row. A ramp laid ACROSS the hill
  is level along its width: down a slope such pieces step (the first delivery's half-pipe).
- A roof whose gable should sit flush on the wall with the eaves hanging past it: size = the wall's own, `over: 1.2`, `keyUnder` = the soffit's sheet.
- A blocker that is only a look (a tower's leg): mark its square in `ctx.taken` and add `feat({ k: 'wall', ..., ghost: true, rail: false })` over it.
- The probe and the board: `hq.skateIssued(true); hq.skate(true); dev.press('w', true)` rides; on the software GPU the game steps 1.4 times a second, so
  a ride goes nowhere. Swap `dev.renderer().render` for a no-op while it rides (probe-fast.js does the same during the load) and sample `dev.walk()`.
- The weight of a prop is not in the catalogue. A Meshy file of about 2 MB is 100,000+ triangles (`coffee_mug`, `coffee_table`, `mini_fridge`, `hook_rail_long`,
  `potted_plant`); the pack pieces are a few hundred to a few thousand. The Christmas pack's `xmas_snow_pine*` are 9,600 to 12,900 triangles a tree (the zone's
  snow tree zones and the Black Run wear them); the retro trees (`pine`, `tree_2`, `tree_3`) are 600 to 900. Count a file: read the GLB's JSON chunk and sum
  each primitive's index accessor `count / 3`.
- Measure the frame rate on the LAST view of a probe run, after a 15 s view of the same place: the first seconds are before the models are in.
- Tree kinds on snow: `pine` (a conifer, 600 triangles) and `xmas_snow_pine` / `_2` / `_3`. `tree_2` and `tree_3` are summer LEAF trees, wrong here.
- An arch part with no `key` is an untextured shape (his rule: generated shapes are always textured): give every part a sheet (`marble_light` takes any tint).
- A sign read from behind: the same `a.sign` again with `{ ry: 180 }` at the other face's z.
- LIGHTS: a room gives a light to the first ten props that carry one, in the room's prop order (HQ_PROP_LIGHT_MAX); the Mountains room has 39. A later
  `flood_mast`, `brazier` or `campfire` shows its glow and flame but lights nothing. Do not count on a real light in a district file after P and K.
- AIR: export `airZones(ctx)` from a district file (bake-mountains.js, 11-16; fields x0, y0, x1, y1 in room squares): kinds dust, embers, fireflies, snow,
  rain, spores, ash, motes. A room with zones draws only its zones: K.js hands the room's own thin snow back as a whole-room zone.
- FPS in a probe: count requestAnimationFrame over 10 s at a fixed view and read `dev.renderer().info.render` (calls, triangles). The frame rate is the
  software GPU's (about 1.5): only good against the same view before the change.

### THE FULL TREES (2026-11-15, mondo: "im not liking how these trees have the 2d cutouts for the leaves ... use the trunks and branches from the current trees ... make better leaves ... texture them with the current tree leaves ... just try to make them natural looking"; he picked row 2 of `woods_tree_leaves_3.jpg`)
- **What they are**: `bake-trees.py` (repo root, Blender through `pip install bpy`) takes a Retro Tree Pack tree and bakes `<name>_full.glb` beside it on R2
  (`Assets/world/nature/retrotreepack/GLB/`). The trunk and bark are the file's own. The two crossed whole-crown cards are gone; in their place are many small
  sheets wearing pieces of THE SAME leaf picture (same material, MASK 0.5, so three-renderer.js treats them as leaves with no code change). Leafy tree: per bough a
  small crossed core + 18 ragged sprays turned so the picture's solid side is inward and its real leaf edge is the outline. Fir / pine: 16 tiers of bough sheets, each a
  slice of the picture from the stem to its real outline, + the picture's middle strip crossed up the stem. About 500-600 triangles a tree (the cards were ~100).
- **Kinds** (data.js HQ_TREE_KINDS): tree_52 full oak, tree_53 full birch, tree_54 full tall birch, tree_55 full spruce, tree_56 full pine. ASSET_MANIFEST.json lists the five files.
- **The Woods** wears them everywhere: bake-woods.js `FULL` maps tree / tree_2 / tree_3 / tree_4 / pine to the full twins (feature trees and the thicket's `kinds`).
  The bare trees (tree_5, dead_tree) stay. No other room changed; the old kinds still draw the cards.
- **Rejected on the way** (his words): solid low-poly clumps "too chunky and low poly"; domed spray balls "the silhouette of the leaves isn't right, especially for the
  winter tree". Mock-up scripts: `/mnt/project-files/world-areas-plan/woods/draw-trees-leaves.py`.
- Not seen in game (no browser run). Cost to watch: the Woods draws about 2,000 thicket trees, so roughly a million more triangles than before (instanced).
- **THE LEAFY ONES AGAIN (same day, mondo: "the ones that are not the winter tree still look really rough, please fix")**: the sprayed leafy crowns are gone. A leafy
  tree is now made exactly like the fir: ten tiers of slices of its own picture from the stem to the real outline (bake-trees.py `fir(..., leafy=True)`), about 300 leaf
  triangles. Same three file names, new bytes; ASSET_MANIFEST.json carries the new shas (the `?h=` fetch). Lesson: slices of the whole picture read natural, loose sprays do not.
- **THE OAK AGAIN (same day, mondo: "the one on the very left looks bad, the rest are good")**: the oak's picture is wider than tall, so whole stem-to-outline slices
  were great flat boards. bake-trees.py form `oak`: twelve tiers, more boughs a tier standing steep, each slice cut into an inner and an outer sheet with their own
  tilt and turn, the crown pulled in to 82 % and started 10 % higher so the trunk shows. About 470 leaf triangles. The other four trees are byte-identical.
- **THE PAINTED TREES (same day, replaces all of the above; mondo: "the undersides of the trees are all black. the new trees mess up dirt paths in the woods bc the
  leaves start too low ... Not these shitty looking paper machete trees ... AAA game. leaves on branches. Anime Ghibli style. simple yet effective")**:
  `bake-trees.py` was rewritten and needs no Blender (`pip install numpy pillow`). Same five file names (`<name>_full.glb`), same kinds (tree_52-56), so the Woods
  wears them with no change to bake-woods.js or the room. Nothing is cut from the pack's crown pictures any more:
  - THE WOOD: a trunk with real boughs and twigs (tapered tubes) in the pack tree's own bark picture. Oak: forks at 36 % into five boughs + twigs + three leaders.
    Birch: one stem with side boughs from 46 % up. Fir / pine: one stem.
  - THE LEAVES: a leafy tree carries round PUFFS at its bough ends (a ball of 8-11 small sheets facing outward, tilted every way). A fir carries ten tiers of
    drooping bough sheets + a shorter shade layer under each tier.
  - THE PAINT: the sheets wear leaf sprays DRAWN by the tool (512 x 384, four sprays x three tones: sunlit, mid, shade) in the pack tree's own green (the mean of its
    picture). A sheet on top of a puff wears the sunlit row, one underneath the shade row: the crown reads round and painted in any light.
  - THE NORMALS + THE ONE-SIDED LEAF: a sheet's normals point out of its puff and a little up. The leaf material is named `ewleaf_<tree>` and is ONE-SIDED in the
    file, with both windings written. three-renderer.js `_foliageGlbMat` reads that (`painted`): draws it FrontSide (two-sided would flip the normal on a back face,
    which was the black underside) and lifts the shade with the leaf's own picture (emissive 0.2 x the tint). Old pack trees are untouched (their leaf is two-sided).
  - THE CLEARANCE: the tool lifts any sheet that would hang under 40 % of the tree's height (fir / pine 30 %) and prints `lowest leaf N% up`. A 6 m tree clears 2.4 m.
  - Cost: oak 460 wood + 648 leaf triangles, birch 288 + 396, fir 36 + 872, pine 36 + 600 (leaf counts are both windings). Files 155-190 KB (were 0.2-1.6 MB).
  - Seen in the game (playtest_city.js on `site_prebuilt_fairy_forest_plots`, birch / oak / fir quarters, from a path and looking up). Lessons: the first trunks were
    twice too fat at Woods heights (a 13 m oak) and the first greens washed out pale in the game's light: keep the picture's values low (sunlit 0.56, mid 0.41, shade 0.27).
  - **EVERYWHERE (same day, mondo: "much better, can you use these trees everywhere, I guess except for the palm trees")**: data.js HQ_TREE_KINDS `tree`, `tree_2`,

"add a remote island with a volcano and unconnected tribe (eventually will make models for)" (plan 4 = plan 3 + the Volcano Island); the plain
plot labels "fine for now"; the Beach Huts "walk ins"; the old rooms "fine for now, but the plan is to eventually cut those pvp maps from these
new areas".

- **THE ROOM** `site_prebuilt_bermuda_beach` (site `prebuilt_bermuda`, part `beach`, "THE BEACH"): 14 x 10 plots of 12 x 12 squares (588 x 420 m),
  written by `node bake-beach.js [--dry-run]` from `docs/areas/beach/layout.json` (plan 4) between `BEACH140-BEGIN / BEACH140-END` in data.js.
  Never hand-edit between the markers. `BEACH_DUMP=1` prints the walked map. The layout is made by `docs/plans/world-zones/make-beach.py` (from
  plan 2's squares) and drawn by `draw-beach.py`.
- **FOUR DISTRICTS:** THE SHORE (14 plots, the west coast off Bayside: the Boardwalk, the Tide Pools, the Beach Huts, the Surf, the Palms, the
  Lifeguard Hut, the Dunes, the Sandbar, the headland sands north and south), THE HARBOUR (8: the Quay and its shed, the Breakwater and the
  harbour light, the Long Pier from the sand to the ship, the Flying Dutchman, the skiff jetty, the Channel's buoys), THE OCEAN (93: open water,
  the Volcano Island far north with the tribe's village, two unnamed islets, the ocean pack's animals), THE BERMUDA TRIANGLE (25: a right
  triangle with sides 6, 8, 10 plots; DOOR_MASTER "it's a right triangle", Room 345. West point = the Lighthouse Rock, right angle = the island
  (the Jetty, the Cay, the Lagoon, the Island Beach), north point = the Maelstrom; inside = the Reef, the Wreck Islet, the Sandbar).
- **A SEA ROOM, AND THE HEIGHTS ARE THE MAP:** `terrain.sea { y: 0 }`, no `gen` (the old Bermuda sea room's way: the whole field is walked, waded,
  swum or sailed; the skiff and the swimmer are the game's own, HQ_SEA_RULES). Everything is `terrain.slope.cells`: sand rises 0.3 m a square from
  the waterline up to its plot's cap (level 0 = 0.6 m, 1 = 1.2 m, 2 = 2.0 m), the sea floor falls 0.7 m a square from the sand (two squares of
  wade, then a swim, 3.5 m deep in open water), dunes to 3.6 m. HARD squares keep four equal corners and so stand as a step: the piers 0.6, the

## THE BEACH, THE DISTRICT FILES — one thread per district (2026-11-16)

mondo 11-16: "every single zone needs to be like that. now. so we can work in parallel". The Beach is written the way Disaster City is
(bake-disaster-city.js "THE DISTRICT FILES"): the districts' content left `bake-beach.js` for one file per district, loaded through one hook.

- **THE FILES** `docs/areas/beach/districts/`: `S.js` The Shore (14 plots), `H.js` The Harbour (8), `O.js` The Ocean (93), `T.js` The Bermuda
  Triangle (25). Each starts with its brief: its plots, what stands there today, what is missing or never seen on screen, the hooks.
- **THE HOOKS** (all optional, every stage runs S, H, O, T): `tailor(ctx)` before the heights (the plan's squares: a plan building `B` you
  build goes back to its ground; only the basics are on `ctx` yet: `cell`, `setRect`, `plot`, `Pxy`, `LIGHT`, the grid sizes), `build(ctx)`
  (walk-ins with `ctx.building`, drawn things with `ctx.look`), `place(ctx)` and `dress(ctx)` (props, palms, people, scatters: `P`, `dec`,
  `afloat`, `swimmer`, `under`, `palm`, `native`, `feat`, `props`), `reach` (squares the walk check must reach from the city door).
- **THE DICE:** each (district, stage) throws from its own start (`DICE` in the tool = the one stream's state at that point before the split).
  A district's new throws never move another district's things; inside your own hook, add at the END to move nothing of your own.
- **WHAT STAYS IN THE TOOL (shared, nobody edits it without a note at the bottom of claims.md):** `bake-beach.js` and `layout.json`; the
  height map and every height rule (sand, sea floor, pier, quay, rock, cone); the sea, the paint, the shell / sky, the west edge; the Flying
  Dutchman's berth, the pier's length and the gangway (`SHIP`, `PIER_END`, `GANG`, `terrain.moored`); the `quay` door to the city and the
  spawn; the links' places (`MAEL`, `POOL`, `BAY`, the tape at `LIGHT`) and the check of their five data.js rows; the helpers on `ctx`; the
  walk check; the room's own rows (label, lines, plots). Need a new helper, a new square letter, a new height rule or a moved door: write a
  note on the board, then make that one change in its own small PR (or ask the thread that holds the tool row).
- **THE RULES FOR A DISTRICT THREAD:**
  1. One thread = one district file. Take that district's row on `docs/notes/claims.md` in your own PR; free it (with one line on its state)
     when you stop. Never edit another district's file, the tool or the layout.
  2. Your scope: your district's exteriors, interiors, dressing, atmosphere and polish, on your own plots. A thing that crosses into another
     district's plots (the Long Pier runs into the Ocean's) stays with the file that has it today.
  3. Never hand-edit data.js between `BEACH140-BEGIN / BEACH140-END`. Edit your file, run `node bake-beach.js` (`--dry-run` = counts only;
     `BEACH_OUT=<file>` writes the block to a file to diff; `BEACH_DUMP=1` the walked map; `BEACH_DICE=1` the dice starts).
  4. **When another district landed first** (always assume one did): `git fetch origin main && git merge origin/main` right before you rebake
     and again right before you merge your PR. A conflict inside the baked block is NEVER resolved by reading it and NEVER by keeping one side
     wholesale: take either side of the block to get past the merge, keep BOTH sides of everything else, then run `node bake-beach.js`. The
     tool rewrites the whole block from the four files, so the rebake IS the merge. Bump the `?v=` token again if main bumped it (RULE #1b).
  5. data.js is an R2 file: every rebake that changes it = token bump + `node sync-zip.js --upload` in the same PR (RULE #1 / #1b).
  6. A browser run is allowed for what you can only judge by looking (RULE #1c, through `probe-fast.js`). This room is big: read the probe
     lessons in "THE BEACH ON PLOTS" (keep only the props near your views with `--pre=`, never `EW_NO_MODEL_QUEUE` on the whole room).
  7. Keep PRs small and land them fast; what you learn goes in this file under your district's own heading, and in your file's header when it
     changes the brief (a thing seen on screen comes off the "never seen" list).
- **PROOF OF NO CHANGE (this split):** `BEACH_OUT` before and after the split is the same file byte for byte (277 645 bytes, sha256
  8a5c015d…), and it equals the block in data.js; data.js did not change, so nothing was uploaded and the token was not bumped. No browser run.
- **KNOWN TO BE THIN (for whoever holds the tool row):** the walk check's own list still names the Shore's and the Harbour's places in the
  tool (a district adds its own with `reach`); `place` and `dress` are two passes only because the content was written in two deliveries.

## THE BEACH IS PART OF DISASTER CITY — the Shore stands on the city's own north beach (2026-11-16, second side, the Shore pilot thread)

mondo 11-16: "I think the issue is that the beach is supposed to be a part of the city, like how we connected the hills", then "the city has its
own beach and you just made a beach, its supposed to be the same ... fix it. combine it ... use the best elements from both. make it bigger".
The city had a thin north beach (six umbrellas on a 7-square shelf under a sea wall drop) and the Beach zone had the Shore in its own sea room
behind a door. STEP 1 (this delivery): the Shore stands IN `site_prebuilt_downtown_streets`, on that north beach.

- **ONE FILE, TWO ROOMS, NEVER TWO BEACHES' WORTH OF CODE:** `docs/disaster-city/districts/W.js` (letter W, the waterfront) runs the Beach
  zone's own district file `docs/areas/beach/districts/S.js` on the city's sand: it hands S.js the same helpers bake-beach.js does (its own
  copies of `sheet`, `building`, `put`, `look`, `P`, `dec`, `palm`, `native` ...), with the same dice per stage, so every hut, prop and palm is
  the same. An edit to S.js changes both rooms: run BOTH `node bake-disaster-city.js` and `node bake-beach.js`.
- **WHERE:** the Shore's square (sx, sy) = x 259 + 3.5 sx, z -252 + 3.5 (sy - 24). Its rows 24..71 (the wild beach and its camp, the Boardwalk
  spur + gate, the Tide Pools, the three huts with the snow cone stand, the Surf, the Palms, the Lifeguard Hut, the court) lie along
  Entertainment from the Hills' Cove to the mole. 39 rows, 196 props, 9 people. Bayside's own beach south of the mole (pier, pavilion,
  towers, yachts, grill) is untouched: one beach, 336 m.
- **BIGGER:** B.js `EAST` 20 -> 32 (the room is 42 m wider east; the centred shell adds the same dead strip west, under the forest as before).
  On the north stretch the sand is 17 squares wide at the boardwalk's own level and falls under the sea past square 163; the sea wall drop,
  its four ramps and its rail are gone there (B.js beach(): two `rect` rows, `RAMPS_N = []`); the stretch's six umbrellas, chair, boat and
  buoys are replaced by the Shore's.
- **HEIGHTS (the trap):** the tool lifts every `arch` row and every prop typed 1 m up or more by the plot levels' height, and the strip beside
  Entertainment carries that district's 8.75 m though its ground is cut to 0. W.js `last()` takes it back off its own rows. S.js reads
  `ctx.GROUND` (0 here, 1.2 in the sea room) for a hung prop's height. The Shore's rows carry ids `shore:*` and are left out of the urban
  decay, sign-font and exterior polish passes (bake-disaster-city.js, one regex beside the Hills').

  Entertainment's sea wall, the lifeguard hut and court with the skyline behind, the long view down the beach, the snow cone stand's inside,

  `pool` row is filled again by the beach's cut); the gate's city side reads DISASTER CITY but stands under a blank 8.75 m sea wall with no
  stair up to Entertainment (the north beach never had one: you come along the boardwalk).
